#+title: Regenerate a generated file that is in conflict
#+description: The shell recipe inventory is generated; when it conflicts during a rebase, take either side and regenerate it rather than merging it by hand.
#+type: memory
#+memory_subtype: project
#+level: cross
#+filetags: :memory:project:
#+created: 2026-09-26
#+updated: 2026-09-26

A generated file in conflict is resolved by taking either side and re-running its generator, never by editing the conflict by hand, because a hand-merged generated file is wrong in ways no gate compares against.

*Why:* The shell recipe inventory (doc/recipes/shell/shell.org) conflicted on three separate rebases of the same branch, and git could not even parse the hunks on one of them. Taking the upstream side and running regenerate_shell_recipe_inventory.py produced the correct file every time, and the inventory gate confirmed it. A capture already exists on main recording the same defect: shell-recipe-inventory-ships-conflict-markers.

*How to apply:* Check out either side, run the generator, verify no conflict markers remain, then stage. The generators are projects/ores.codegen/scripts/regenerate_shell_recipe_inventory.py for the recipe index, regenerate_cmake_component_files.py --component <full-name> for the component source lists, and render_component_draft.py or check_component_drift.py for generated code. The same rule applies to a component_files.cmake: regenerating beats merging, and the component's #+full_name: is what the script takes, not the directory.
